claim: Governed delegation joins an assignment to relevant knowledge, durable work, and acceptance evidence. Context selection is bounded and advisory. Dispatch gates act on assignment structure and resolved phase state; completion review evaluates landed work and independent evidence. Recovery preserves existing artifacts before work is reassigned.
topology: The work order and component/constraint models feed bounded context selection. Lifecycle policy and reconciled phase state feed the dispatch decision: is the assignment authorized? A refused assignment does not execute without repair or a valid override. An authorized agent preserves durable work, which is both inspected at completion and evaluated by independent checks. Checks produce review evidence; the completion decision asks whether obligations are satisfied. Interrupted or unresolved work is inspected and reconciled before redispatch. Absence of state is not evidence of DONE.
bw_encoding: Rectangles identify models and artifacts; rounded boxes identify mechanisms, and diamonds mark admission decisions. Gray identifies flexible reasoning only. Heavy outlines mark consequential application/admission boundaries. Solid arrows carry data, models or results; dashed arrows carry verification/challenge or subordinate selection relations.
redesign: Author-approved moderate redraw aligns the two governance decisions with equal heavy diamonds. Independent checks produce review evidence; durable work also reaches completion review. Refusal, positive DONE and recovery semantics remain.
